study_title: Binder Optimization with LLMs and Specialized Models (TNKS2 Small-Molecule Lead Optimization)
authors: Ishaan Ganti (Rowan Scientific)
regime_label: LLM generation + specialized oracle filter / sequence model
benchmark: TNKS2 scaffold decoration (32 ligands/round, RBFE ddG kcal/mol)
metric: Top-1 / Top-5 RBFE ddG (more negative = tighter)
llm_model: GPT-5.6 Sol / Claude Opus 5 (1-shot -> 4 rounds RBFE feedback)
llm_score: 1-shot: GPT-5.6 Sol -5.44, Opus 5 -3.22 (-4.09 no RDKit); Round 4: GPT-5.6 Sol -9.23, Opus 5 -5.80 (-6.86 no RDKit); F85Q control drops fluorinated para site from 24/32 -> 1/32 (GPT) & 18/32 -> 4/32 (Opus)
notes: F85Q pocket-mutation control cleanly proves LLMs respond to 3D pocket geometry rather than only reciting PDB TNKS2 inhibitors. However, specialized baselines were restricted to 1-shot with imposed site priors (where CReM and FLOWR beat LLMs), and all scores rest on computational RBFE (cycle-closure RMS error 2.59 kcal/mol) on one scaffold.

authors: Meghana Kshirsagar, Allen Nie, Ching-An Cheng, Fanglei Xue, Rahul Dodhia, Juan Lavista Ferres, Kevin K. Yang, Frank DiMaio

study_title: GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models
authors: Masatoshi Uehara, Edward Zhou, Joshua Park, Morgan Griffiths, Austin Clyde, Suyash Shringarpure, Yuan Yuan, Kevin Rao, Anton Bushuiev, Michael Yu, Kathryn M. Collins, Jesse Hendricks, Puwanat Sangkhapreecha, Lee-Shin Chu, Sharrol Bachas, Joy Jiao (OpenAI Life Science Team and Onava AI)
regime_label: LLM generation + specialized oracle filter / sequence model
benchmark: Nonpublic minibinder & IL-4Ra VHH backbones (Onava wet lab, 1 uM BLI)
metric: Single-dose BLI hit rate & dose-response KD
llm_score: 123 minibinder hits across 5 targets (MDM2 75/88=85.2%, VEGF-A 26/42=61.9%, IL-7Ra 5/18, PD-1 8/59, PD-L1 9/89; 38 hits at 30-50% parent ID); 128/182 (70.3%) IL-4Ra VHH hits (median 46.0% CDR ID; VHH 054/150 KD 10.3-21.8 nM at 17/25 mutations)
baseline_model: No matched wet-lab ProteinMPNN / AbMPNN control
notes: Strongest evidence in the paper: nonpublic backbones rule out parental binder memorization, and 17/25 CDR mutations retain 10-22 nM binding. Confounded by heavy 3-model ensemble filtering (9,902 VHHs passing ESMFold2 distilled to 184 tested), single-dose BLI noise, and missing matched MPNN wet-lab control.

study_title: Guided Inverse Folding with LLMs
authors: Ishaan Ganti (Rowan Scientific)
regime_label: LLM generation + specialized oracle filter / sequence model
benchmark: 5 PDB backbones (4 post-cutoff June-Aug 2026) at 70%/50%/40% identity caps
metric: ESMFold2 + Boltz-2 refolding pass rate (plot-only, no scalar table)
llm_model: GPT-6 Astra / GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-5.6 Terra / Claude Opus 5 (with 4 example sequences)
llm_score: Zero-shot failed; with 4 examples GPT-6 Astra leads and produces passing designs at 50% (and 27AH 40% cap: 28/82 ref match); Opus 5 struggles even on 9TLN
baseline_model: ProteinMPNN (supplied 3/4 examples; no head-to-head pass rate reported)
notes: Post-cutoff Gly-stripped backbones control memorization well, showing zero-shot fails without examples while guided redesign succeeds down to 40-50% ID; confounded by ProteinMPNN seed examples, lack of inter-round ID caps, asymmetric Claude timeouts, and missing no-feedback control.
